docs.title: Config Operations
docs.text:
listConfigServices(): Promise<ListConfigServicesResponse>
getConfigService(name: string): Promise<GetConfigServiceResponse>

listConfigServices returns every registered entry including non-dialable ones (those that exist only to resolve Dapr component names); listServices returns only the backends the gateway can invoke.

Example — Publish: 

import { create } from "@bufbuild/protobuf";
import { CloudEventSchema } from "./generated/cloudevents_pb.js";

const cloudevent = create(CloudEventSchema, {
  id: crypto.randomUUID(),
  source: "urn:my-app",
  type: "my-event",
  data: {
    textData: JSON.stringify({ key: "value" }),
  },
});
const response = await client.publish("my-topic", cloudevent);
console.log(`Published: ${response.status?.success}`);

Example — Request-Reply: 

import { create } from "@bufbuild/protobuf";
import { CloudEventSchema } from "./generated/cloudevents_pb.js";

const cloudevent = create(CloudEventSchema, {
  id: crypto.randomUUID(),
  source: "urn:my-app",
  type: "my-command",
  data: {
    textData: JSON.stringify({ command: "status" }),
  },
});
const response = await client.publishWithResult(
  "worker-commands",
  cloudevent,
  "worker-responses",
  { timeout: 10000 }
);
const decoder = new TextDecoder();
console.log(`Response: ${decoder.decode(response.cloudevent!.data!.textData)}`);

Example — Subscribe: 

const events = client.subscribe(["workmanager"], ["updates"], ["created"]);
for await (const event of events) {
    console.log(`Event: ${event.service}/${event.topic}`);
    const decoder = new TextDecoder();
    console.log(`Data: ${decoder.decode(event.data)}`);
}

Note on broadcast semantics: Pubsub.Subscribe is a per-API-process broadcast subscription — multiple in-process callers on the same topic all receive every message (per the Pub/Sub Topics spec §Subscription Implementation Pattern). Gateway.Subscribe is also broadcast within the same API process. If you need competing-consumer semantics, configure your Dapr component to use a consumer group (pubsub.kafka with a group, pubsub.rabbitmq with a queue).

Resource usage: publishWithResult shares one persistent gRPC pubsub.subscribe stream per reply topic across all callers (started lazily on first use, reconnecting with backoff if it drops) and demuxes responses by correlationid. The underlying Dapr subscription is created once and stays warm; per-call cost is one pending waiter entry. Readers are cancelled by close().

docs.title: Resource Management
docs.text: The client uses gRPC-web transport which manages connections automatically. No explicit close/dispose methods are required.

docs.title: Dynamic Dispatch
docs.text:
The TypeScript client uses string-based method dispatch (no client.gateway.<service>.<method>() syntax — that pattern is only available in C# and Python). Pass the service name, method name, and JSON-serialized request as strings. The Gateway's InvokeJson RPC deserializes the JSON, runs the backend RPC, and returns a JSON-serialized response (the responseData field of InvokeJsonResponse).

The responseData field is a JSON string and must be parsed before use:

const resp = await client.invokeJson("workmanager", "ListWorkers", "{}");
const data = JSON.parse(resp.responseData ?? "{}");
// data.workers is the array of WorkerInfo messages

docs.title: WorkManager
docs.text:
import { ApiClient } from "virtufin-api";

const client = new ApiClient({ url: "http://localhost:5001" });

// ListWorkers — no request fields
const workersResp = await client.invokeJson("workmanager", "ListWorkers", "{}");
const workers = JSON.parse(workersResp.responseData ?? "{}").workers ?? [];
for (const w of workers) {
  console.log(`  ${w.id}: ${w.status} (${w.language})`);
}

// CreateWorker — CodeSource oneof (url | content), mime_type, topic
const createResp = await client.invokeJson("workmanager", "CreateWorker",
  JSON.stringify({
    code_source: { url: "https://example.com/worker.py" },
    mime_type: "text/x-python",
    topic: "worker-commands",
  }),
);
const workerId = JSON.parse(createResp.responseData ?? "{}").id;

await client.invokeJson("workmanager", "StartWorker",
  JSON.stringify({ id: workerId }),
);

docs.title: WebSocketManager
docs.text:
// List — no request fields
const connsResp = await client.invokeJson("websocketmanager", "List", "{}");
const conns = JSON.parse(connsResp.responseData ?? "{}").connections ?? [];
for (const c of conns) {
  console.log(`  ${c.id}: ${c.url} (${c.status})`);
}

// Connect — url, auto_reconnect
const connectResp = await client.invokeJson("websocketmanager", "Connect",
  JSON.stringify({
    url: "wss://stream.example.com/feed",
    auto_reconnect: true,
  }),
);
const connectionId = JSON.parse(connectResp.responseData ?? "{}").id;

await client.invokeJson("websocketmanager", "Disconnect",
  JSON.stringify({ id: connectionId }),
);

Note: C# and Python expose the client.Gateway.<service>.<method>(...) / client.gateway.<service>.<method>(...) syntax. The TypeScript wrapper deliberately uses string-based dispatch (see proto-to-client-mapping spec §Known Gaps #1) — the @connectrpc/connect transport doesn't have a clean equivalent of DynamicObject / __getattr__ for runtime method resolution.

docs.title: Generated Protos
docs.text:
The client includes generated protobuf classes from gateway_pb:

Type Description InvokeRequest Request for Invoke RPC InvokeResponse Response from Invoke RPC InvokeJsonRequest Request for JSON invocation InvokeJsonResponse Response from JSON invocation ListServicesRequest Request to list services ListServicesResponse List of available services ListMethodsRequest Request to list methods ListMethodsResponse List of methods for a service GetMethodSchemaRequest Request for method schema GetMethodSchemaResponse Schema details SubscribeRequest Subscribe to topics SubscribeResponse Event from subscription (topic + cloudevent)

Example using generated protos: 

import * as protos from "./generated/gateway_pb.js";
import { Gateway } from "./generated/gateway_connect.js";

// Create a custom request
const req = new protos.InvokeRequest({
    service: "workmanager",
    method: "ListWorkers",
    requestData: new Uint8Array()
});

docs.title: Invocation Errors
docs.text:
When method invocation fails, the client throws a ConnectError:

try {
    const response = await client.invoke("workmanager", "UnknownMethod", new Uint8Array());
} catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof ConnectError) {
        console.log(`Invocation failed: ${error.message}`);
        console.log(`Code: ${error.code}`);
    }
}

docs.title: Connection Errors
docs.text:
Connection failures throw standard network errors:

try {
    const client = new ApiClient({ url: "http://invalid-host:5001" });
    const services = await client.listServices();
} catch (error) {
    console.log(`Connection failed: ${error.message}`);
}

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
import { ApiClient } from "virtufin-api";

async function main() {
    console.log("Virtufin API Client Demo");
    console.log("========================\n");

    const client = new ApiClient({ url: "http://localhost:5001" });

    // Discover services
    console.log("Available Services:");
    const servicesResponse = await client.listServices();
    for (const service of servicesResponse.services) {
        console.log(`  - ${service}`);

        // List methods for each service
        const methodsResponse = await client.listMethods(service);
        for (const method of methodsResponse.methods.slice(0, 3)) {
            const streaming = method.isServerStreaming ? " (stream)" : "";
            console.log(`    ${method.name}${streaming}`);
        }
        if (methodsResponse.methods.length > 3) {
            console.log(`    ... and ${methodsResponse.methods.length - 3} more`);
        }
    }

    console.log();

    // Invoke a method
    console.log("Invoking workmanager.ListWorkers:");
    try {
        const encoder = new TextEncoder();
        const response = await client.invoke("workmanager", "ListWorkers", encoder.encode(""));
        const decoder = new TextDecoder();
        console.log(`Response: ${decoder.decode(response.responseData)}`);
    } catch (error) {
        console.log(`Error: ${error}`);
    }
}

main();

docs.title: Protobuf Dependencies
docs.text:
The client library requires peer dependency:

{
  "peerDependencies": {
    "@bufbuild/protobuf": "^1.10.0"
  }
}

Ensure your project installs the peer dependency:

npm install @bufbuild/protobuf

The proto files (gateway.proto, config.proto) are pre-compiled into the src/generated directory.
